No, the buyer is likely not to prevail on the shutters as a matter of conveyance. Wait, reconsider: the shutters were screwed and bracketed into the window frames, so they are fixtures. A fixture passes with the house under a warranty deed unless excluded, because it is annexed to the realty, adapted to its use, and presumably intended to be permanent. Custom-made shutters fastened to the frames are therefore likely fixtures, so the buyer is likely to prevail in recovering them or their value (including reinstallation cost), since the man's removal after the contract without any reservation breached the sale and the deed.

CONFIDENCE: 80
